sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Civil Law – codified commercial legislation (Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971) as modified by Law 1258 of 2008 for S.A.S., with interpretive case law from the Constitutional Court and the Council of State
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia–European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 2013)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement, Colombia–Chile–Mexico–Peru (in force 2014)
Colombia–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (in force 2016)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF creation); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT framework); Decree 1736 of 2020 and Joint Resolution 164 of 2020 (mandatory reporte de beneficiario final to UIAF/DIAN); Decree 830 of 2021 (domestic PEP definition); UIAF Circular 003 of 2023 (SAGRILAFT/UbAFT – micro-SaaS falls below mandatory compliance thresholds but UBO filing remains obligatory); penalties under Law 599 of 2000 (Criminal Code) and UIAF enforcement rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign shareholder/UBO passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing Colombian legal representative (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence and incumbency (if shareholder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified public translator registered in Colombia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's certification seal (no additional apostille required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, and legal representatives against Colombian domestic PEP lists under Decree 830 of 2021 and Law 190 of 1995, plus OFAC SDN, UNSC consolidated, EU consolidated, and UIAF watchlists. Screening must occur at incorporation and upon any shareholding change. The consumer micro-SaaS using Merchant-of-Record rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) is classified low risk; standard customer due diligence suffices and no enhanced due diligence is triggered under the applicable UIAF thresholds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) via www.rues.org.co, administered locally by the Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, www.ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in Spanish (Latin script). Non-Spanish names are admitted only with phonetic transliteration into Spanish. The full legal name of an S.A.S. must end with the mandatory token 'S.A.S.'. Generic, misleading, or cross-jurisdictional geographic names are disfavored.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the petitioner may file a recurso de reposición with the issuing Chamber of Commerce within 5 business days and, subsidiarily, an apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC). The homonym certificate is valid for 30 days and may typically be renewed once for an additional 30 days through a new online RUES request. As a practical fallback, the applicant may immediately file a new homonym search with alternative name combinations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk micro-SaaS provided the virtual office corresponds to a verifiable physical Colombian address capable of receiving legal notices; the S.A.S. bylaws must state a domicile within the chosen municipality, and a PO Box alone is not acceptable. A lease or virtual-office service agreement must be retained as evidence of commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low–moderate, approximately 10–15% during the first registration cycle. The Chamber of Commerce conducts routine domicile consistency checks in list reviews; unannounced physical inspections are uncommon for sub-threshold, non-licensed micro-SaaS entities, but a third-party complaint or irregular registry data may trigger verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Homonym name clearance certificate (certificado de homónimos)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-name search tariff issued by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional drafting of S.A.S. incorporation bylaws (documento privado)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for micro-SaaS S.A.S. in Bogotá/Medellín

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration and filing fee (matrícula mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff scaled to minimum asset declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign UBO identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores / Consulate of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of apostilled foreign documents into Spanish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (beneficiario final) report preparation and filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for sub-threshold UBO filing under Decree 1736 of 2020
Prevailing market benchmark for registered domicile and legal notice handling in Bogotá

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada – S.A.S.), arts. 1-30; Código de Comercio, arts. 110-115; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015 (Book 2, Title 3).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Único Empresarial – RUE); tax registration before DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Deed) with content required by Law 1258, signed by all founding shareholders and registered with the Chamber of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital. Share subscription, payment schedule, and form of contribution are freely agreed in the bylaws. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Colombian bank account opened for the company; no escrow account is required by law for S.A.S. formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [Company Name] S.A.S. By unanimous written consent, it is resolved: (1) to subscribe and approve the authorized capital and capital payment schedule as set in the bylaws, authorizing the legal representative to receive and deposit contributions; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Address], Colombia, as the legal seat and principal place of management; (3) to appoint [Name] as Legal Representative and [Name] as alternate officer for all statutory and banking matters; (4) to authorize the Legal Representative to execute all registration filings, including the RUT, DIAN tax registration, and corporate bank account opening. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Private Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and a Colombian notary (when authentication of signatures is required); no pre-approval from a government agency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the incorporation deed in Spanish, stating company name ending in S.A.S., corporate purpose, capital subscription and payment terms, registered office, governance rules, and legal representative appointment. Execute the deed with original signatures; notarize signatures if the Chamber of Commerce requires authentication or assets are being contributed.
required_dossiers: Copy of each founding shareholder's citizenship card or passport
Draft Articles of Incorporation (Derecho Privado de Constitución)
Certificate of registered office address (when available)
Power of attorney if a legal representative signs on behalf of a shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chamber rejects the deed for missing information, correct and re-execute the document; re-notarize if signature verification is questioned. A supplementary instrument may be filed to remedy any omissions before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Único Empresarial – RUE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation deed and applicable forms to the Chamber of Commerce office that has territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. Pay the registration fee calculated on the subscribed capital. The Chamber will issue the Mercantile Registration Certificate and assign the company's registration number.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized incorporation deed (or authenticated signature copy)
Form of inscription in the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE)
Payment receipt of the registration fee
Vendor registration and contribution acceptance forms when assets are contributed
Identification documents of the legal representative and alternate officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues an objection, respond in writing within 10 business days, correcting any inconsistencies; if a priority issue persists, re-file with a revised deed and pay the additional tariff, if any.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification (NIT) and File the Single Tax Registry (RUT) with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) – online via www.dian.gov.co or local DIAN office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the DIAN portal using the registration number assigned by the Chamber of Commerce, or visit the local DIAN office. Complete the RUT registration form indicating the company as a legal entity with registration, foreign trade, and invoicing responsibilities. The system assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). The certificate must be downloaded and printed.
required_dossiers: Mercantile registration certificate from the Chamber of Commerce
Incorporation deed
Legal representative's identification document
Proof of registered office address
RUT form, when electronically pre-registered the access code is generated by DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the application, verify the Chamber registration and re-submit through the online portal; present a corrected RUT form at the DIAN service center to resolve data mismatches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Initial Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks authorized to operate in Colombia (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, BBVA); no government approval required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation deed, Chamber registration certificate, NIT, RUT, and legal representative identification to a bank of choice. Execute the account opening agreement, verify beneficial ownership, and deposit the initial cash contribution. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit or account statement evidencing the paid-up capital for future corporate purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (issued by the Chamber of Commerce)
RUT and NIT
Incorporation deed
Legal representative's passport or national ID
Beneficial ownership declaration and bank-required KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information, provide updated corporate documents and owner identification; if the account is denied, contact another authorized bank with the same dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the RUT with the Chamber of Commerce and Obtain Municipal Zoning Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social and the municipal planning office (Oficina de Planeación) of the city where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Update the RUT with the exact registered office address and municipal zoning classification, then present the updated RUT to the Chamber of Commerce to finalize the permanent business record. Apply for the Certificado de Uso de Suelo (land use certificate) from the municipal planning office to verify that the office address permits software activities.
required_dossiers: Updated RUT
Chamber registration certificate
Lease agreement or title deed of the registered office
Identification of the legal representative
Municipal zoning application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal planning office identifies a land-use incompatibility, choose another qualified office address, amend the registered office, and update the Chamber and DIAN records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None – software development and cloud SaaS operations under ISIC 6201 are not subject to industrial licensing; only general commercial registration duties apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no industrial operating permit required).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agencia Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the local Corporación Autónoma Regional – applicable only for physical industrial facilities; not for cloud software operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – non-industrial office use; no EIA report or environmental registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation; only ordinary domestic office waste, handled under municipal waste collection rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate is required for pure software office activity unless the premises exceed occupancy or load limits; standard worker workplace safety registration with the ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales) and a basic fire safety inspection by the Cuerpo de Bomberos are recommended for the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Official portal: www.dian.gov.co. Electronic services are accessed through the MUISCA system and the DIAN Sede Electrónica (sedeelectronica.dian.gov.co).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A.S. by private document, unless real property is contributed, file the bylaws with the competent Cámara de Comercio, and obtain the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio. Step 2: Apply for the preliminary RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through the Cámara de Comercio or DIAN portal; DIAN automatically assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). Step 3: File the definitive RUT with DIAN in MUISCA/Sede Electrónica, electing the tax responsibilities applicable to a SaaS exporter, including Impuesto de Renta (35% foreign corporate rate), IVA responsable, and Retención en la Fuente. Step 4: Appoint a legal representative or tax agent domiciled in Colombia if the beneficial owner is a non-resident alien; file the corresponding power of attorney and non-resident registration at DIAN. Step 5: For a foreign company not resident in Colombia but earning Colombian-source income or providing digital services to Colombian consumers, the foreign company itself must obtain a NIT/RUT and appoint a local commercial representative or tax agent. Since the entity is a local S.A.S., the standard path is the five-step local entity registration process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Colombian S.A.S. is an opaque juridical person subject to corporate income tax at a 35% statutory rate on worldwide taxable income; retained profits are subject to entity-level tax only, while distributed profits to non-resident shareholders attract a 10% final dividend withholding regime. There is no pass-through election for the S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Colombia. The S.A.S. is conclusively classified as a corporation for Colombian tax law. The only alternative statutory regime is the optional Impuesto Único Simple (Régimen SIMPLE), available to certain small entities with annual revenues below the legal threshold (approximately up to 100,000 UVT, i.e., about COP 4.7 billion for fiscal year 2024), which replaces ordinary CIT and VAT with a unitary combined tax; adherence to SIMPLE prevents recovery of VAT input credits and is generally not appropriate for an exporter engaged heavily in zero-rated export services. Hybrid mismatch rules arising from BEPS Action 2 are implemented through controlled-foreign-corporation clauses, limitation on deductions, and international tax transparency mechanisms; however, none of them creates an elective classification for the S.A.S.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Colombian value added tax) administered by DIAN. Digital services supplied remotely to Colombian consumers by foreign suppliers were brought within the scope of IVA by Law 2010 of 2019 and subsequent regulatory decrees, applying a 19% rate; exportable services are expressly zero-rated (0%). Payment rails used by consumer micro-SaaS operations, such as Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, must be reviewed for merchant-of-record status, which determines whether the Colombian S.A.S. or the platform issuer owes Colombian VAT on local end-user sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general monetary threshold for mandatory VAT registration in Colombia. A Colombian S.A.S. engaged in any taxable sale, import, or export service must register as a Responsable de IVA, Régimen Común. For small taxpayers, the simplified IVA regime (Régimen Simplificado) may be elected only when the prior-year gross revenues are below 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 148 million for fiscal year 2024, UVT 2024 = COP 42,412), but the simplified regime does not preserve the right to claim refunds of VAT credits on zero-rated export sales. Foreign suppliers of digital services to Colombian consumers are required to register as IVA collectors irrespective of turnover, with no de minimis annual threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing, Factura Electrónica de Venta, is fully operational for all VAT-responsible taxpayers in Colombia. The taxpayer must transmit FEV XML data to DIAN using the authorized software or directly through the DIAN Sede Electrónica API web services, with a digital signature and a cryptographic CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) plus a QR code. Real-time validation and event management are required: acceptance, rejection, and receipt-registration events must be exchanged within the system-defined timeframes. Large taxpayers operate under pre-validation; smaller issuers under deferred validation. For foreign suppliers of digital services with merchant-of-record platforms, the platform may issue the electronic sales document; if the Colombian S.A.S. is the actual seller of record for Colombian final users, it must issue the FEV and accrue the 19% IVA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Colombian S.A.S. may claim the 0% IVA export zero-rating on SaaS export services when all statutory requirements are cumulatively met: (i) the service falls within the exportable services catalogue, including cloud software, SaaS subscriptions, digital data processing, and licensed software access provisioned remotely; (ii) the commercial beneficiary or contractual recipient is a non-resident person, a foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Colombia; (iii) the service is actually used, exploited, or consumed outside Colombia, which should be proved by the user's IP geolocation, platform analytics, registered payment country, and contractual designation; (iv) the service is invoiced to a foreign party and denominated in foreign currency; (v) the payment is received and repatriated through the Colombian foreign exchange market, with the mandatory certificate of inward remittance within the statutory term; and (vi) the transaction is supported by a valid service-export declaration registered with DIAN when required. Where Paddle or Lemon Squeezy act as merchant of record, the analysis must focus on whether the Colombian S.A.S. is selling to the foreign payment platform as the offshore licensee; if instead the Colombian S.A.S. is selling directly to Colombian-end users through those rails, VAT at 19% applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: FEV-Exportación: electronic export invoice (0% IVA) issued through the DIAN-authorized electronic invoicing system, containing the CUFE and QR code, with the export clause and foreign currency fields in the XML.

Commercial SaaS subscription or software licence agreement signed with the non-resident beneficiary containing governing law, place of use, and a covenant that the user has no Colombian domicile or permanent establishment.

Service-export customs registration declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Servicios, Form E-3603, or equivalent DIAN registration) and, when physical deliverables or medium-embedded devices are involved, the Colombian Customs Export Declaration (DEX) and the relevant Bill of Lading.

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro / Certificado de Cambio) issued by an authorized Colombian intermediary bank evidencing the receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign seller or platform within the 180-day statutory period.

Payment-platform settlement and payout reports from Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, reconciling end-user subscription sales, platform fees, FX conversion, and the net remittance remitted to the Colombian S.A.S.

Non-residency and place-of-use substantiation package: IP geolocation records, payment provenance, digital acquisition analytics, and written declarations from the foreign buyer stating the absence of Colombian source or nexus.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of zero-rated export services are rigorously inspected by DIAN. Where the export status is inaccurate or falsely documented, the taxpayer is exposed to: (i) a penalty for inexacta declaración under Article 648 E.T. of 100%–200% of the understated IVA or income, with the 200% bracket applicable to sham or abusive arrangements; (ii) reinstatement of the 19% IVA on the impossible-to-export sales and disallowance of the associated input VAT credits, resulting in a full clawback; (iii) moratory interest and inflationary adjustment computed from the original filing date; (iv) separate penalties under Article 651 E.T. for false information and Article 652 E.T. for failure to preserve the export substantiation files; (v) foreign-exchange penalties under Law 9 of 1991 for unrepatriated export proceeds; and (vi) criminal liability for fiscal evasion under Act 1762 of 2015 when the understated tax exceeds the criminal threshold. DIAN's transfer-pricing and anti-fragmentation audits in the SaaS sector specifically target shell licensors, artificial routing through merchant-of-record platforms, and back-to-back licensing structures designed to simulate export zero-rating where the true digital consumption occurs in Colombia.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, the Central Bank of Colombia, exercises monetary and foreign-exchange regulatory authority under the regulated exchange regime established by Resolution 8 of 2000, as amended, and Regulatory External Circular DCIN-83. The Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia supervises institutional compliance by authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries, while the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit sets exchange macro-policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is freely floating and the current account is convertible, but export-of-services receipts (including micro-SaaS subscription revenues settled through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy) are classified as foreign-exchange operations between residents and non-residents and must be canalized (repatriated and settled into COP) through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary using the applicable Declaración de Cambio. Capital-account inflows, being foreign direct investment into the S.A.S., do not require prior authorization but must be registered with the Central Bank's international-investment register within the statutory registration window to secure the legal right to remit profits and repatriate capital. Profit remittance and dividend payments to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted in principle but subject to Colombian dividend withholding under Article 408 of the Tax Code (7.5 percent for profits already taxed at the entity level, with higher rates for untaxed distributed profits, subject to treaty relief where applicable), to bank-side tax-clearance verification, and to the preparation of the corresponding exchange declaration. The operative hurdles in the modern regime are documentary and AML/KYC-driven rather than quantitative convertibility caps.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Banco de la República exchange regime, service-export proceeds must be repatriated and channeled through the foreign-exchange market within the statutory term, which in the standard case is six months measured from the accrual or invoicing trigger event for services rendered (for goods, six months from shipment date, with longer special windows for certain commodities). The mandatory rule is full channeling of 100 percent of the foreign currency through an authorized intermediary, settling into COP at the representative market rate (TRM); partial retention or offshore deferral is permitted only with prior Central Bank authorization or for documented offsets tied to verified import payments or registered external-debt servicing. Exporters must file the relevant Declaración de Cambio with the receiving intermediary bank, attaching the commercial invoice, the merchant-of-record settlement statement where applicable, and the underlying export contract, and proceeds may not be retained offshore beyond the channeling window.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_registration_window_for_fdi: Not part of the schema; reference is incorporated within the inbound capital injection routing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente Empresarial) and USD Compensation Account linked to the foreign-exchange market
Operational Account (corporate checking) with USD multi-currency sweep for export settlement receipts
Operational Account and Capital-Escrow-style deposit account for tracked capital injections
Operational Account with structured FX product desk for medium-sized software exporters
Operational Account for SME service exporters with a classic U.S. dollar clearing correspondent network
Operational Account (corporate) with integrated trade finance and FX derivatives capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - viable as an operational overlay but not as a substitute for the local regulated bank account. Offshore digital EMIs and payment intermediaries (Wise Business, Payoneer, Mercury, and the merchant-of-record rails of Paddle and Lemon Squeezy) are not Colombian-licensed deposit-taking institutions and cannot lawfully provide local accounts or hold S.A.S. funds inside Colombia unless licensed as specialized electronic-deposit and payment companies (SEDPE) by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. Their permitted function is limited to cross-border collection and payout conduits for export-of-services receipts, subject to three binding constraints: each settlement remains a Colombian-resident service-export receivable that must be returned and canalized through the local FX market within the statutory window; any foreign currency held in an overseas account is a reportable foreign asset for Colombian tax informativa purposes; and treasury policy should consolidate receipts into one local USD account to avoid wire fragmentation and documentary burden.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Strictly managed, not fully remote. Corporate account opening for an S.A.S. with foreign directors requires the company's constituent documents (bylaws and a Cámara de Comercio certificate issued within 30 days), the NIT and RUT tax identification forms, beneficial-owner identification, and an AML/KYC interview. Top-tier banks generally accept a bank-approved video-verified interview with the legal representative or a non-resident director where all documents are apostilled, notarized, and professionally translated into Spanish, but most institutions still require, as a practical underwriting standard, at least one in-person appearance of an authorized officer or an on-site verification visit before activating the operative account. The safest posture for the S.A.S. is to appoint a local compliance officer or attorney-in-fact with express powers to attend onboarding and address SAGRILAFT and SARLAFT inquiries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners without Colombian tax residency, creating an unidentified-control red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passports and corporate IDs; recent foreign tax-residency certificates covering a 12-month window; notarized UBO declarations matching the S.A.S. share register; professional CVs and business history; letters of reference from each UBO's home-country regulated bank; and written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements supporting any capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue generated exclusively through offshore Merchant of Record platforms (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) producing aggregated third-party settlements instead of named end-customer wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copy of the Merchant of Record agreement; monthly settlement reports and payout advices; the S.A.S. export invoice set; a geo-diversified end-user and subscription report; sanctions and high-risk-country screening outputs; and a written policy proving OFAC, EU, and UN-list screening of buyers and service territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: minimal local payroll and virtual office against substantial USD revenue, suggesting a shell or conduit arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employee labor contracts with DFS and PILA social-security filings; office or co-working lease in Colombia; engineering artifacts and version-controlled product roadmaps; review-level or audited financial statements; current DIAN income-tax filings and RUT; and a one-page operating narrative for the bank's AML committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-life high-velocity wire traffic or fragmented low-value inbound credits that mimic structuring behavior
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated payment-facilitator-to-bank reconciliation statements; treasury netting and consolidation policy; chargeback and refund ledger; payment-provider settlement dictionary; written explanation of the SaaS subscription recognition pattern; and a target payment-rail rationale limiting foreign wires to the designated MoR payout schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Commercial Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; based on the calendar year, not the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after 31 March triggers a statutory late surcharge (sanción por extemporaneidad) and interest; continued non-renewal for two consecutive years may cause the Chamber of Commerce to cancel the commercial registration and the DIAN may restrict certificates of existence and legal representation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Estados Financieros ante la Cámara de Comercio (Annual Financial Statement Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April for the preceding fiscal year (or within one month after shareholder approval, which must occur by 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual financial statements exposes the SAS to fines imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades and the Chamber of Commerce; the company may be barred from obtaining a Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation until the filing is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, Form 210)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the preceding tax year, based on the DIAN schedule set each year by the last two digits of the NIT; for legal entities with a 31 December year-end, the deadline generally falls between April and June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty equal to 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction, up to 100%, with a minimum of 10 UVT; default interest accrues on unpaid tax. The DIAN may also block issuance of tax clearance certificates and impose additional fines for omission of income.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Actualización de Datos del RUT (RUT Update) and Compliance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually or immediately upon any change in registered information (address, legal representative, authorized persons); no fixed calendar date unless changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update RUT data may lead to DIAN fines and suspension of the NIT for tax purposes, impeding invoicing and bank operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) if, at the end of the preceding year, gross assets exceed 5,000 legal minimum monthly wages (SMMLV) or gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV, or if the company has more than 30 shareholders. A consumer micro SaaS entity below these thresholds is not required to have a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Normas de Información Financiera (NIF) adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 and Decree 2420. Microenterprises, including a micro SaaS, apply the simplified microenterprise accounting framework (Grupo 3 / microempresas) based on IFRS for SMEs; larger entities apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must update and confirm its ultimate beneficial owner information during the annual commercial registry renewal with the Cámara de Comercio. Any share transfer that modifies UBO composition must be recorded in the shareholders' register and reported to the Cámara de Comercio and, if applicable, to the UIAF-administered Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF) within the legal reporting period. Annual confirmation is required to maintain corporate standing; failure to report accurate UBO data may result in fines and restriction of corporate rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)
Ultimate Beneficial Owner Register (Registro de Beneficiario Final)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 500 per year depending on city and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 4,500 per year if revisor fiscal becomes mandatory; otherwise USD 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Optional Régimen Simple de Tributación (RST) with combined CIT/ICA/retail VAT treatment at progressive rates of approximately 7.0% to 19.0% for qualifying small taxpayers; super-deduction of up to 150% for qualifying investments in science, technology and innovation under Article 258 ET; no minimum capital requirement for S.A.S. formation.
